Marissa / Emily — legal here. Below is proposed MSA language that addresses BrightWorks' concerns while keeping Redwood's ability to reference customers for PLG/sales motion. Please review and tell us any hard stops.

Proposed publicity clause (MSA, section X.Y):

"Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, non-transferable right to reference Customer as a Redwood customer in Redwood's marketing materials, including Redwood's website and sales collateral. Prior to public distribution of any press release or joint announcement referencing Customer, Redwood shall provide Customer with a draft release and obtain Customer's written approval, not to be unreasonably withheld. Customer shall have five (5) business days to review and respond to Redwood's draft. Logo usage shall comply with Customer's brand guidelines and shall be limited to the uses expressly authorized in the Order Form. Redwood shall not disclose Customer's confidential pricing, usage volumes, or personally identifiable information in any public materials.

Either party may revoke the publicity permission upon thirty (30) days' written notice, during which Redwood shall cease any further public use and remove all reasonable public-facing instances of Customer's logo or quote.

"No Endorsement": Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer's name or logo shall not be used in any manner that implies endorsement of Redwood's products or services beyond the factual statement that Customer is a customer of Redwood.

We also recommend adding a checkbox on the Order Form where Customer explicitly opts into the publicity permission and uploads or confirms the correct logo asset. That helps procurement and avoids future disputes.

If BrightWorks insists on a longer review period, please provide suggested language; 5 business days is typical for our customers and helps us meet go-to-market timelines.

—Laura
Counsel, Redwood Inference
